questions.q: Who does Lipton say came closer to the truth about evolution, decades before Darwin?
a: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
Gregor Mendel
Alfred Russel Wallace
Charles Lyell
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that the French biologist Lamarck, working a few decades earlier, described evolution more accurately than Darwin.

questions.q: What role does Lamarck give to cooperation between species?
a: It is central to how evolution works
It plays no part in natural selection
It slows down adaptation to change
It matters only for plants and microbes
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts Lamarck's emphasis on cooperation with Darwin's survival of the fittest, and says modern science supports Lamarck.

questions.q: What did Lipton conclude about genes after his realization in the Caribbean?
a: The environment controls a cell's life and genes are only blueprints
Genes alone decide our health and personality
The environment matters only after birth
Cells are unaffected by their physical surroundings
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes Lipton's insight that a cell is controlled by its environment, with genes acting as blueprints the environment reads.

questions.q: According to Lipton, what shapes a child before birth?
a: The mother's diet, surroundings and emotions
Only the father's genetic contribution
The family's income and level of education
The child's own early choices and habits
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a fetus's cells perceive the mother's diet, environment and emotions, and are programmed by them.

questions.q: What hopeful conclusion does the summary draw from Lipton's work?
a: We can rewrite even the programs installed early in life
Early influences can never be changed later
Biology is fixed from the moment of conception
Only childhood therapy can undo early damage
questions.why: Lesson 3 ends by noting that later in life we can still rewire even the earliest-installed programs, which the summary calls its most optimistic point.
